paraphrase: One who renounces in due order performs the Vaiśvānara sacrifice, places the fires in himself, tells his son 'you are the sacrifice, you are all' (or without a son departs east or north), begs among the three higher varṇas, uses the hand as bowl, stays one night in a village, five in a town, four months in the rains; his thread is meditation on the Self, his topknot knowledge; for him there is no night or day.

checks.note: E-text chapter (adhyāya, khaṇḍa or section) 1 located; the passage matches the paraphrase (it begins: 'athātaḥ sannyāsopaniṣadaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ | yo'nukrameṇa sannyasyatisa sannyasto bhavati | ko'yaṃ sannyāsa…').

paraphrase: After the forty saṃskāras, one who has dispassion may renounce; three are called fallen — who makes a renouncer fall, who makes a fallen one renounce, who obstructs renunciation; the ineligible (including the leprous and the unbelieving) may renounce only when sick unto death.

paraphrase: Activity is of two kinds, 'of the cat' and 'of the monkey'; the text assigns them to those devoted to knowledge and practice (construal uncertain).

paraphrase: One who repeats twelve thousand praṇavas daily sees Brahman shine within twelve months.

paraphrase: 'Abandon dharma and adharma, abandon truth and untruth; having abandoned both, abandon that by which you abandon.'

paraphrase: Food: fill half the stomach with food, a quarter with water, leave a quarter for air; fasting is better than eating at night, unsolicited food better than fasting, alms better than unsolicited food.

paraphrase: When the sun sees a renouncer it trembles, thinking 'he will pierce my orb'; one who renounces saves sixty generations before and after; the fire of the renunciation declaration burns faults.

paraphrase: Five kinds of alms: mādhūkara (a little from several houses like a bee), prākpraṇīta (arranged in advance), ayācita (unasked), tātkālika (what comes at the moment) and upapanna (brought to him); mādhūkara may be taken even from a mleccha, never food from a single house.
